With a familiar name of this scale confirming its schedule early, market participants across the sector now have a fixed point on the calendar around which commentary, expectations and sector comparisons begin to cluster. Scheduling notes of this kind are routine in form yet meaningful in effect, since they signal that a vast body of operating data is about to be made public. These threads give market observers plenty to track as the quarter is formally closed out and presented. The broader mood around energy names has also sharpened the focus. With crude benchmarks swinging on supply decisions abroad and demand signals reading as mixed, each major update is being parsed for clues about how the largest producers are weathering the environment. ExxonMobil ranks among the largest integrated energy companies anywhere, spanning exploration and production, refining, and a sizeable chemicals arm. That integrated structure means the business captures value across the entire chain, from the wellhead through to refined fuels and petrochemical products that feed countless downstream industries. The company operates across several continents, with a portfolio that blends long-life conventional assets, large offshore developments and a fast-scaling unconventional presence. The upstream arm remains the engine of the group, and the company has leaned heavily on a small number of advantaged basins to drive volume growth. The Permian in the American Southwest sits at the heart of this effort, bolstered by the earlier combination with a major Permian pure-play that lifted the group's acreage and barrels in the region. Management has repeatedly framed these advantaged barrels as central to how the company lowers unit costs while lifting overall output. Offshore Guyana continues to stand out as one of the most closely watched developments in the global energy map. The company leads a consortium on the prolific Stabroek block, where a sequence of production vessels has been brought online in stages, steadily ramping the nation into a meaningful source of crude on the world stage. Together, the Permian and Guyana form the twin growth engines that shape much of the group's production narrative. The pairing of onshore unconventional scale with world-class offshore volumes is frequently cited as the backbone of the company's barrel growth across the current decade. What makes the Guyana story distinctive is the low cost and high quality of the crude being lifted, which places these barrels among the most economic in the global portfolio. The downstream business, grouped under the product solutions banner, converts crude into fuels, lubricants and other finished goods. For a company whose production increasingly flows from Texas acreage, situating the corporate center nearer that activity reads as a deliberate alignment of structure with operations. Proximity to the Permian heartland can tighten the link between corporate decision-making and field operations, and it places the company closer to a dense cluster of energy expertise, suppliers and talent. The move caps a long arc in which the state has grown ever more central to the group's barrels, its spending and its strategic planning. ExxonMobil has been among the most active participants in that wave. The energy sector faces no shortage of headwinds. Commodity price swings remain the single largest source of uncertainty for earnings, and refining and chemical margins can compress quickly when supply outpaces demand. Regulatory shifts and permitting timelines add further complexity to large project planning. Currency moves, shipping costs and the pace of global economic growth all feed into how a company of this scale performs from one period to the next. These variables form the backdrop against which the coming third-quarter disclosure will be read and compared with peers. Weather events, refinery turnarounds and unplanned outages can also sway a given quarter, introducing short-term noise into the numbers. The companys performance also offers a window into the broader energy sector, where commodity prices, global demand, refining conditions, and operating costs can shape market sentiment. ExxonMobil is an integrated energy company involved in finding and producing crude oil and natural gas, refining petroleum, manufacturing chemical products, and marketing fuels and lubricants. This contrast highlights why a companys performance cannot be understood through a single financial measure. Sales reflect activity across the business, but they do not necessarily show how effectively that activity translates into earnings. Production costs, refining margins, commodity prices, maintenance expenses, and product demand can all influence the difference between sales and earnings. The company also reported a stronger per-share earnings result compared with the same period in the previous year, according to the supplied source. That comparison provides additional context, although quarterly results can fluctuate with changes in crude oil and natural gas markets. The key question is whether operating performance remains resilient when commodity prices and refining conditions change. Consistent production, cost management, and disciplined capital allocation can help shape the companys financial performance across different energy-market environments. ExxonMobils integrated model spans upstream, downstream, and chemical operations. Upstream activities include exploring for and producing crude oil and natural gas. Downstream operations include refining crude oil into fuels and other petroleum products, while its chemical business manufactures materials used in packaging, automotive components, construction, and consumer products. This structure provides exposure to several parts of the energy value chain. Stronger crude production can support upstream activity, while refining margins influence the performance of fuel-related operations. Chemical demand and manufacturing conditions can create another source of variation. At the same time, integration does not eliminate exposure to commodity cycles. Lower energy stock prices can affect production economics, while weaker demand or narrower refining margins may place pressure on other business areas. Operational reliability, project execution, and capital requirements also influence performance. ExxonMobil recently announced a quarterly dividend, continuing its role as a company that distributes cash to eligible shareholders. Dividend payments can be an important part of the company's financial profile, particularly for readers who focus on recurring distributions. However, a dividend should be assessed alongside the cash required to maintain operations, develop resources, manage debt, and support capital projects. The payout ratio can help describe how much of a companys earnings is allocated to dividends, although it does not provide a complete picture of cash-flow coverage. Energy companies also face changing capital requirements. Exploration, production facilities, refining assets, and infrastructure require ongoing spending. Commodity-price changes can affect cash generation, making financial flexibility an important factor when evaluating the durability of distributions. Readers comparing dividend-paying companies may find the concept of  dividend yield useful for understanding how a dividend relates to a securitys market value. A rising market price can reflect improved expectations, stronger demand for energy, or wider market conditions. title: ExxonMobil (NYSE:XOM) Hits New 1-Year High - Still a Buy? - MarketBeat
content:
ExxonMobil Corporation (NYSE:XOM - Get Free Report) shares reached a new 52-week high during trading on Monday. The stock traded as high as $183.75 and last traded at $181.99, with a volume of 11,514,954 shares. The stock had previously closed at $183.21. A number of research firms recently weighed in on XOM. Bank of America lowered shares of ExxonMobil from a "buy" rating to a "neutral" rating and boosted their price target for the stock from $154.00 to $158.00 in a research report on Tuesday, July 28th. title: Why Did XOM, COP, CVX Jump To 52-Week Highs Last Week? - Stocktwits
content: Shares of energy companies Exxon Mobil Corp. (XOM), ConocoPhillips (COP) and Chevron Corp. (CVX) surged to annual highs on Friday as oil prices rallied to a six-month high amid growing geopolitical tensions. Brent crude futures maturing in December climbed over $116 per barrel on Friday, while U.S. West Texas Intermediate (WTI) crude futures for December rose to $102.40 per barrel. Last week, Houthi attacks on Saudi Arabia intensified, stoking fears about energy security and infrastructure and shipments across the Middle East. Saudi Aramco evacuated its Dhahran headquarters after attacks in the country's eastern oil-producing region. While U.S. President Donald Trump said last week that Washington would not be negotiating with Tehran and suggested further developments could follow soon, on Sunday, he ruled out an attack on Iran this week. Meanwhile, though oil shipments through the Strait of Hormuz have recovered toward pre-war levels in recent weeks, with the U.S. Central Command aiding passage through the critical waterways, Citigroup analysts have warned that the recent improvement in shipments may not represent a sustained recovery. UBS analyst Giovanni Staunovo also reportedly told Reuters that any further escalation could trigger renewed supply disruptions. Brett Erickson, Managing Principal at Obsidian Risk Advisors, said in a post on X over the weekend, “Iran is currently launching missiles and drones at vessels attempting to transit the Strait of Hormuz. Despite the preparations from all sides to ready for a full-scale resumption of the war, Iran does not intend to allow the U.S. to use this window to flow out excessive amount of oil and refined products in the meantime.” Exxon Mobil, ConocoPhillips and Chevron surged to 52-week highs on Friday amid the steep climb in oil prices. XOM stock hit a 52-week high of $183.75 during trading hours on Friday, closing nearly 3% higher. COP stock rallied to a 52-week high of $152.77 during regular trading, and ended 3.5% higher at close. CVX stock surged to a 52-week high of $ 233.74, closing up nearly 3%. On Stocktwits, retail sentiment around XOM and CVX stocks was ‘bullish’ at the time of writing, while it was ‘bearish’ for COP. XOM stock has gained more than 49% year-to-date, while COP and CVX stocks have surged nearly 56% and 50%, respectively. For updates and corrections, email newsroom[at]stocktwits[dot]com. Shares of AST SpaceMobile (ASTS) slipped 0.4% overnight late Sunday even as the company sought more spectrum to expand its satellite broadband capabilities, while market veteran Herb Greenberg questioned its valuation despite a steep selloff. ASTS stock jumped nearly 3% on Friday to close at $39.70, but ended the week down 2%, marking its fourth consecutive weekly decline. In a Friday statement, AST’s unit, AST & Science, proposed adding Q/V and E-band service-link capabilities to its 248-satellite network. The links would connect satellites directly to customer terminals, broadening its proposed high-frequency operations beyond ground-gateway connections. The request covers selected frequencies between 40 and 51.4 GHz, plus downlinks at 71 GHz -74 GHz and uplinks at 81GHz –84 GHz.  “This supports a deployment model in which the smallest terminal classes can be used by functional mobile user equipment with varying bandwidths, powers, and antenna sizes,” AST said. The proposed services would require compatible terminals alongside AST’s core connectivity offering for standard smartphones. “AST SpaceMobile’s operations are not solely dependent on use of the E-band; AST SpaceMobile will utilize other spectrum, including the Q/V-band and 700/800 MHz bands, for its user terminals in addition to the E-band spectrum,” the filing said. Approval and interference coordination are still necessary, including protections for military users in certain bands. Meanwhile, Greenberg, a veteran financial journalist and investment researcher, questioned AST’s realistic profit potential despite its expanding addressable market. He noted that shares had lost over half their value over six months and recently hit a 52-week low. “Even with that, it’s still priced as if it’s the hottest thing ever, especially when compared with its more established Satcom peers,” he said. Greenberg highlighted an enterprise valuation of 140 times trailing revenue, versus 38 times for Globalstar, 7.5 times for Iridium and three times for Viasat. He also noted a trailing EBITDA loss of about $532 million. “Drilling deeper, based on trailing multiples, you wouldn’t know that its network is nowhere near fully built out yet,” he said. He highlighted multiples of 16 times estimated 2028 revenue and 324 times estimated 2028 adjusted EBITDA, based on $1 billion in revenue and $50 million in adjusted EBITDA. Greenberg acknowledged that a “sky-high valuation” alone rarely justifies avoiding or shorting a stock, while highlighting high short interest and Fidelity’s warning of securities-lending stress. AST is targeting initial, intermittent coverage before year-end in the United States, Canada, Japan, the United Kingdom and Saudi Arabia, subject to regulatory approvals. Continuous service will require more satellites. “We are moving toward service with the partnerships, spectrum and network capabilities needed to bring cellular broadband from space into people’s everyday lives,” President Scott Wisniewski said. The company has more than 60 gateways deployed, installed or planned, supporting over 60 mobile operators whose networks reach more than three billion subscribers. It targets 100 MHz of U.S. spectrum access and 5,600 activated coverage cells before year-end, up from over 3,000. Meanwhile, its smartphone-focused network has shown peak downloads of 98.9 Mbps, with next-gen satellites expected to reach about 200 Mbps. In Europe, Deutsche Telekom, Orange, Telefonica and Vodafone are exploring a joint mobile-satellite spectrum bid, with a satellite provider yet to be selected. On the other hand, Viasat has challenged an earlier AST overseas-spectrum application as “fatally flawed” over interference and allocation concerns. SK Hynix (SKHY) is considering a special dividend of 16 trillion won ($12 billion), funded by gains from its investment in Japanese memory-chip maker Kioxia Holdings, South Korea’s Dong-A Ilbo reported Monday, citing unnamed investment banking sources. The payout would amount to about 80% of an estimated 20 trillion won in gains SK Hynix booked from its Kioxia investment in the first half of 2026. The company is expected to announce its plans alongside third-quarter earnings on Wednesday, according to the report. SK Hynix’s Seoul-listed shares rose marginally in Asian trading hours on Monday morning, while the U.S.-listed stock was up over 1% in overnight trading late Sunday. SK Hynix said it was reviewing options to return money to shareholders but had not decided on a special dividend, according to a Bloomberg report, which added that the prospect of a payout has helped the stock hold up amid a broader selloff in AI-related shares. SK Hynix joined a Bain Capital-led consortium in 2018 to acquire Toshiba’s former memory-chip business for $18 billion. Kioxia’s value climbed following its Tokyo stock-market debut in 2024. While Bain Capital sold its entire stake earlier this year, SK Hynix still holds convertible bonds linked to an investment vehicle with about a 14% stake in Kioxia, according to Bloomberg. Last week, SK Hynix scrapped plans for a U.S. IPO of its Solidigm flash-memory subsidiary. In an Oct. 23 statement, the South Korean chipmaker cited capital-market conditions and share-price trends behind its move. The IPO had reportedly targeted a $10 billion to $15 billion raise and a valuation of up to $150 billion. The decision follows a sharp correction in U.S. and South Korean semiconductor stocks. That's better than Apple. 200 fast. 300 in 2027.” SKHY stock closed at $137.02 on Friday and remains 8% below its Nasdaq listing price. Additionally, the U.S. Central Command said on X that the commander of CENTCOM, Brad Cooper, visited the Strait of Hormuz on Oct. 25, as U.S. forces have helped Gulf partners export more than 1.5 billion barrels of crude oil since summer. CENTCOM also said it had helped more than 3,000 commercial vessels successfully transit the Strait over the last six months. "Today, primary transit routes in the Strait of Hormuz remain free and clear of Iranian sea mines thanks to incredible efforts by our people," said Cooper. "We remain intensely focused on keeping commercial traffic flowing as we work with our teammates in the U.S. interagency, Gulf Cooperation Council, and shipping industry." Oil prices pulled back from six-month highs overnight. Brent crude futures were trading at $114.85 a barrel, down 1.60%, while WTI crude futures traded nearly 2% lower at $101.28 per barrel. Meanwhile, as election season takes off worldwide, Trump reaffirmed his endorsement of Benjamin Netanyahu in the lead-up to the Israeli elections. “To the people of Israel, to those who haven’t seen it, I am attaching the Endorsement I gave one week ago to your Prime Minister, Bibi Netanyahu,” he said in a post on Truth Social. In Brazil, leftist President Luiz Inacio Lula da Silva defeated right-wing Senator Flavio Bolsonaro in a surprising turn of events, sending Brazilian stocks lower. Markets will now brace for a busy earnings week, with Alphabet Inc. (GOOGL), Microsoft Corporation (MSFT), and Amazon.com Inc. (AMZN) set to report their earnings. Other key companies set to post their latest quarterly results this week include Verizon Communications Inc. (VZ), Visa Inc. (V), Boeing Co. (BA), and Coca-Cola Co. (KO). The Federal Reserve is also set to begin its policy meeting on Tuesday, and October’s interest rate decision is likely to set the tone for equity and bond markets for the rest of the year. The long-acting IL-23 antibody is being developed for less frequent dosing. In the earlier Phase 2a Everlast-A trial, 63.5% of treated patients achieved completely clear skin at Week 16, rising to 71.4% at Week 28 after doses only at Weeks 0 and 4. Incyte (INCY) follows with an investor webcast on its ESMO cancer findings and pipeline. Highlights include INCB161734, which targets the KRAS G12D cancer mutation in colorectal and pancreatic cancers, and dual-target antibody INCA33890. The findings come from early-stage studies, with separate Phase 3 trials underway. ESMO Congress continues through Tuesday in Madrid. Iovance Biotherapeutics (IOVA) presents Monday on Lifileucel, which uses patients’ own immune cells to fight cancer, in two previously treated soft-tissue sarcomas. The data come from a Memorial Sloan Kettering-led pilot trial. Summit Therapeutics (SMMT) enters the week after reporting positive Harmoni-GI1 results on Sunday. In the China-based Phase 3 trial, Ivonescimab plus chemotherapy reduced the risk of death by 25% compared with Durvalumab plus chemotherapy in advanced biliary tract cancer. Median overall survival was 14.9 months versus 12.1 months at the interim analysis. Novartis (NVS) reports Tuesday, followed by Biogen (BIIB) and GSK on Wednesday. Thursday’s lineup includes Eli Lilly (LLY), Merck (MRK), Bristol Myers Squibb (BMY) and Gilead Sciences (GILD), which reports after the market closes. AbbVie (ABBV), AstraZeneca (AZN), Regeneron Pharmaceuticals (REGN) and Sanofi (SNY) follow on Friday. GSK reports after the recent FDA approval of Hibsago, or Bepirovirsen, its Ionis-partnered chronic hepatitis B treatment. (MPC) surged to annual highs on Monday as oil prices rallied amid growing geopolitical tensions. Brent crude prices touched nearly $110 a barrel on Monday as tensions in the Middle East continued to ratchet up. A series of recent escalations, including attacks on commercial ships near the Strait of Hormuz, Houthi missile strikes on Saudi Arabia, and Ukraine’s strike on a Russian refinery, stoked fears about a further constraint in fuel supplies, sending prices higher. Worries continued despite the U.S. government’s efforts to curtail rising prices, including planned fuel releases and changes to U.S. sanctions on Russian imported fuel. Since the U.S.-Iran war began in February, energy prices have been climbing steadily, boosting energy companies. As per Koyfin data, energy stocks have outperformed the S&P 500 by a significant margin in 2026. Exxon Mobil, Chevron, and Marathon Petroleum shares surged to 52-week highs on Monday before closing lower amid the steep climb in oil prices. XOM stock hit an annual high of $179.30 during trading hours on Monday before closing about 0.4% down. CVX stock surged to a 52-week high of $225.67, but ended the session 0.28% lower. MPC stock rallied to a 52-week high of $493.98 during regular trading, but finished the day nearly 1% down. Retail sentiment around XOM, CVX and MPC stocks was ‘bullish’ at the time of writing on Stocktwits. Retail investors in Sellas Life Sciences (SLS) are floating multibillion-dollar buyout scenarios and steep share-price gains after CEO Angelos Stergiou marked the company’s 15th anniversary with a post about its “next chapter.” SLS stock jumped 5% on Monday to $10.49, snapping three straight losing sessions. In his LinkedIn post, Stergiou reflected on Sellas’ growth from a private startup into a public biotech advancing investigational cancer treatments GPS and SLS009. “Reaching 15 years isn't just about celebrating our history; it is about stepping into our next chapter with even greater focus, drive, and resolve,” he said. He acknowledged past setbacks and thanked shareholders, employees and trial participants, while reaffirming the company’s commitment to patients. “Our mission remains deeply personal, and our promise to the patients we aim to serve is steadfast. We look forward, God willing, to the best chapters that are still to be written with GPS and SLS009,” he added. On Stocktwits, retail sentiment for SLS slipped to ‘bearish’ from ‘bullish’ levels a day ago amid a 258% jump in 24-hour message volumes. One user said: “My opinion, Dr. Stergiou’s message was a master-class at reassuring EVERYONE that all is well.” A user also floated a minimum $40 billion valuation. Another user argued for a $50 billion valuation, calling a $247-per-share figure. A separate user proposed a $120 billion buyout scenario and also predicted a share price of $540-plus. Across bullish share-price predictions, including scenarios tied to clinical results, targets ranged from $100 to over $540. Discussing buyout news in case of favorable data, one user said: “If BO news post good data then there’s no stopping this beast (really no explanation required as it could go full berserker mode).” BO means buyout. Another user challenged the lofty valuations and said: “I will be so glad to get out of this ticker when it hits $15 again.” The CEO’s message comes as investors have been searching for potential deal signals in recent months. In June, a filing disclosed changes to executive severance arrangements, including lump-sum payment provisions for Stergiou. For CFO John Burns and chief development officer Dragan Cicic, qualifying departures within one month before or one year after a change of control would trigger 15 months of salary, the annual target bonus, up to 18 months of health-coverage reimbursements and full vesting of unvested equity. Sellas’ conference plans have provided another talking point. The company is listed at Booth 138, with a 20-by-30-foot space, for the Dec.12- Dec.15 American Society of Hematology (ASH) meeting in New Orleans. Major exhibitors include Eli Lilly, Pfizer, Merck, AbbVie and Bristol Myers Squibb. The booth size has fueled speculation about a partnership or acquisition. Currently, investors are awaiting data from Sellas’ two lead programs. The Phase 3 Regal trial is testing GPS, an immunotherapy targeting WT1, in acute myeloid leukemia (AML) patients who achieved a second complete remission following salvage treatment. Its final-analysis process is triggered by 80 deaths. Sellas reported 78 events as of May 11. Reaching 80 precedes database lock, data review and analysis before results are disclosed. The company also expects fourth-quarter topline data from its 80-patient Phase 2 SLS009 study in newly diagnosed AML, including patients with early resistance to azacitidine and venetoclax. SLS009 is also being explored in pancreatic cancer. Preclinical findings from last month showed 17.9% apoptosis (programmed cell death) in a patient-derived tumor model resistant to Daraxonrasib, versus 2.8% with Daraxonrasib alone. Combining the drugs raised apoptosis to 36.5% and necrosis to 30.6%. For updates and corrections, email newsroom[at]stocktwits[dot]com. Research and advisory firm Gartner recently said in a report that artificial intelligence infrastructure investments are in danger as concerns over bloated AI capex mount. The firm said that as the commercial duopoly for primary frontier models consolidates around Anthropic and OpenAI, the cash flows to meet that massive computing asset base from neoclouds are not scaling proportionally with upfront costs. Meanwhile, major Wall Street analysts are also taking opposing stances on CoreWeave. MoffettNathanson and BNP Paribas lowered their price targets on CoreWeave, while Goldman Sachs took a more positive outlook. MoffettNathanson slashed CRWV stock’s target to $89 from $107 and kept a ‘Neutral’ rating on the shares, citing its “staggering financial obligations.” BNP Paribas also cut its price target on CoreWeave to $117 from $169 and maintained an ‘Outperform’ rating, according to The Fly. The firm said that it sees a continued deterioration in investor confidence amid its debt obligations. While higher financing costs could contain the company's ability to fund future growth, the shares are "seemingly discounting some liquidity concerns," the analyst reportedly said in a research note. However, Goldman Sachs upgraded the stock to ‘Buy’ from ‘Neutral’ and set a price target of $106, implying upside of more than 73% from its last close. The firm said ongoing volatility in the credit market raises questions about whether CoreWeave can finance its next phase of growth, and at what pace. However, Goldman also said the ongoing debate over demand for frontier vs. off-frontier intelligence, and CoreWeave's annual recurring revenue per megawatt and unlevered internal rate of return, are "biased to the upside" over the next 24 months because of tight supply. The analyst also said that CoreWeave is differentiated from other neoclouds.
